[spoiler=[b]Revolution as an institution? | ZJ[/b]]
[list]from: Shangguan Zhenjin <znjasnobres@falaralto.ta>
to: cj111@uq.edu.qi
date: 27 Oct 2028, 08:11
mailed-by: falaralto.ta
signed-by: falaralto.ta
security: high level[/list]

My question then is this, Mr. Cui:

In all communist governments (or which you call "socialist governments", "people's democratic governments", or some other terminology, for you denigrate the designation of "communism" for anything by the final triumph of your cause), there is invariably the use of the term called "revolutionary". A revolution is a great reverberation, if you may agree with my definition. It is to my understanding that all revolutions in history have been called such retroactively, and anything that does not triumph in the moment of disorder is merely a disturbance, some crisis or internal conflict, or else a protest. A revolution is a great changing of the systems of the state inasmuch as historiography may sometimes lament at the time periods before and after its occurrence.

A revolution, therefore, is the moment. When it is over, why still do your governments persist in calling itself the revolution and its supporters the revolutionaries, when the duties that had been ascribed to it at the moment of triumph is now over?

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Semantics and the Purpose of Revolution[/b]]
[list]from: Cui Jin <cj111@uq.edu.qi>
to: znjasnobres@falaralto.ta
date: 27 Oct 2028, 11:03
mailed-by: uq.edu.qi
signed-by: uq.edu.qi
security: high level[/list]

Dear Princess Imperial,

Forgive the semantic argument, but this will be important in my response. A revolution is never simply the changing of the guard, but the long, drawn-out, sometimes terrible, sometimes heroic, and always difficult transformation that comes after, when the people's revolution must now lay down its arms and take up the positions of power to reform the whole of society towards the great and vindictive battle against the imperialist systems upon which this very revolution came about. Until then, the revolution exists as an institution of the new society that changes and continues to change until the classless, stateless society emerges.

Therefore, socialist governments only abandon the term "revolutionary" when one of two things occur: A counter-revolution successfully emerges and reinstates the old tyranny, or else we succeed in forming the new man in a communist society.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Masses =/= revolution? | ZJ[/b]]
[list]from: Shangguan Zhenjin<znjasnobres@falaralto.ta>
to: cj111@uq.edu.qi
date: 27 Oct 2028, 11:15
mailed-by: falaralto.ta
signed-by: falaralto.ta
security: high level[/list]

So a counter-revolution, massed by the common people, perhaps even proletariat, who succeeds in storming through the palace of a socialist government, who overwhelms its regular armed forces through an awesome feat of arms, cannot itself be considered revolutionary?

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Yes[/b]]

[list]from: Cui Jin <cj111@uq.edu.qi>
to: znjasnobres@falaralto.ta
date: 27 Oct 2028, 13:38
mailed-by: uq.edu.qi
signed-by: uq.edu.qi
security: high level[/list]

A counter-revolution, by its very definition, opposes the liberation of the people and the destruction of the old systems. And yet, it is not in my power to proclaim to the counter-revolutions to halt their misuse of the term "revolution", since it is their very purpose to pervert its meaning, nor can I ever guarantee that the proletariat is able to always be a person of complete and total reason, for to presume absolute rationality to all living things is lunacy. In the state of nature we seek our needs, sometimes wretchedly, and once sated we seek our wants, sometimes savagely. Even the proletariat might wage a violent war to restore their own chains if it means successfully retreating into the illusory comforts of the old master. There can be no true revolutionaries except for those that understand the ideals of the communist society.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Single-mindedness in the revolution | ZJ[/b]]

[list]from: Shangguan Zhenjin <znjasnobres@falaralto.ta>
to: cj111@uq.edu.qi
date: 27 Oct 2028, 15:47
mailed-by: falaralto.ta
signed-by: falaralto.ta
security: high level[/list]

So it's the socialist definition to simply reject all other viewpoints as evil. Don't you think that this way of thinking is why the world constantly anathemizes you?

If the revolution is an institution, as in a government persisting through an indefinite period of time until the classless society, and if its mission is to create the 'new man,' then by your own logic, any opposition to that institution is not merely political dissent, but a symptom of false consciousness. You are not compelled to see them as citizens exercising a political will, however misguided. You are compelled to see them as a disease to be cured, or an enemy to be crushed, for the sake of their own future freedom. And then will come soft rains and the dead on the ground, shot to death by your own "revolutionary army", in pursuit of the darkest and most single-minded liberation.

During that long transformation, who decides what the people truly need versus what they merely want in their 'savagery'? If it is always the institution itself, the self-proclaimed vanguard of the revolution, then have you not simply replaced the old master with a new one?

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Discussion and story (last response for now)[/b]]
[list]from: Cui Jin <cj111@uq.edu.qi>
to: znjasnobres@falaralto.ta
date: 1 Nov 2028, 5:56
mailed-by: uq.edu.qi
signed-by: uq.edu.qi]

I will tell you a story, Princess Imperial. It concerns a certain Sanguinian acquiantance I met from way back during my winter stay at Citharo. 

He was a good gentleman, from a wealthy family, who by the excellence of his birth had been destined to inherit a family enterprise that had been in operation since the 16th century. However, man has a tendency to rebel against the path that had been set for him, and this good friend of mine opted to live a life in constant and costly adventure. Princess Imperial, have you ever climbed mountains? I haven't. I think only madmen dare to rise to these hostile hellscapes.

You traverse narrow ridges in the shadow of total darkness, at risk of stumbling and taking out your whole group in the mighty winds, or else straying so far and become entrapped in an airless crevice until you're gone, and many have gone.

Some madmen conquer mountains if to be simply exonerated from the charge of having turned back, and yet here are so many horrible fates that await them. And yet men conquer mountains still, as with this friend of mine, now tired and breathing heavily as he dangles against the jagged rock and stone of Mount Palamina, under which is the eternal abyss, and with great effort he thrusts himself up and he breathes steadily but decides that it was only near to the hour of death that his felt truly alive. Then, it is over. He is fatigued but happy, and while he is content to have triumphed over the challenge that he had set for himself, the dream is over, supplanted in turn by a distant memory. 

I am certain, and will remain certain for the rest of my life, that living in general seems to be predestined towards something approaching misery. Before our time, men savaged the weak and took what was needed to survive. We say now that the primal nature of man has been sated by this thing called civilization, but who determines the civility of societies if not those that have long since triumphed from their conquests? Who have impelled the many to observe this hegemony that is called liberality, which liberates only those with the means and the will to devour the world, now restrained to instead destroy the human race from a distance. 

These "civilized men" take from the labor of the proletariat, they drain the vitality of the workers with the money of their fathers and their father's fathers and reap the great returns for the great merit of their wise investments, while the producers of the goods are let to starve in the cities they've made. 

Therefore, the revolution can only be rationality, and the counter-revolution can only be irrationality.

[/spoiler]
